Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

citelens 0.2.0

New functions

  • abstract_ca() runs correspondence analysis on the terms in abstracts, comparing groups such as periods, venues or sources. It comes with plot() and print() methods.

  • author_network() builds a weighted co-authorship network and reports author-level and network-level statistics, connected components and communities. plot() draws one small map per group of authors, or a single overview. plot_cluster(), plot_clusters() and plot_network_overview() draw individual views, and cluster_maps() saves maps for every cluster to PNG and PDF files. Nothing is written unless you supply dir or pdf.

  • find_duplicate_papers() and dedupe_papers() flag and remove papers that are listed more than once, such as a journal version and a preprint. Matching uses normalised titles with optional edit-distance tolerance, and by default a pair must also share an author surname.

  • citation_rank() ranks papers, venues or authors by citations and reports the h-index, g-index and i10-index for the collection.

Other changes

  • New vignette, “Getting started with citelens”.

  • New sample data, inst/extdata/sample_authors.csv: a small synthetic set of papers used in examples and tests.

  • igraph is now in Suggests. The network functions need it, and they give a clear error if it isn’t installed.

citelens 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-14

  • Initial release.
  • Convert ‘RefWorks’ Tagged Format and ‘RIS’ exports to ‘BibTeX’ (convert_refworks(), refworks_to_xlsx()), and read ‘BibTeX’ into a data frame or ‘Excel’ file (bib_to_df()).
  • Parse saved ‘Google Scholar’ results pages, or a folder of them (scholar_parse_html(), scholar_html_to_bib()), and look up missing abstracts in ‘OpenAlex’ (fetch_abstracts()).
  • Text analytics on abstracts: topic modeling (topic_model() and helpers), cosine document similarity with duplicate finding and ‘Excel’ export (doc_similarity(), similarity_to_df()), and trends over time (word_trends(), topic_trends()), with charts.
